pass_b_english: They were fortifying themselves, keeping themselves outside of all access, and declaring themselves better than the Babylonians.

In another way, the Jewish nation was also being destroyed, having been worn down and plundered, and the remaining ones were being taken; and they were setting up sacred vessels to false gods, and sending away those who had been under the yoke of their slavery.

God spoke through one of the holy prophets, saying, 'What have you to do with me, Tyre and Sidon, and all Galilee of the foreigners? Do you repay me? Do you take vengeance on me? I will quickly repay you, and I will take back my silver and gold, and my chosen and beautiful things, which you took and brought into your temples, and you sold the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel to the sons of the Greeks, so that you might drive them out of their borders' (Isaiah 23:18).
Tyre was an island, with a narrow strait in the middle, and not far from the mainland.
When the Babylonian came, seeking to take it along with the other cities, he ordered his armies to fill in the sea between, to join it to the mainland, and not to leave it an island.

As the Babylonians were about to capture Tyre, the majority of its inhabitants, who were engaged in commerce and accustomed to sailing, took their families and departed from the island to other cities and villages.
Most of the people, including the most prominent ones, escaped with their ships, and the Babylonians were not moderately grieved to learn that they had done so.
The Babylonians then entered the city, killing those who remained, taking many captive, and doing what was customary for victors.

The prophet Ezekiel had foretold this event, and God had spoken to him about the fate of Tyre, saying that Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, had subjected his power to great servitude against the city, but had not received any reward for his labor, and instead, God gave him the land of Egypt (Ezekiel 29:18).
After the capture of Tyre, the Babylonian turned his war against the Egyptian nation.
The prophet Isaiah now recalls this history and commands the ships of Carthage to wail because Tyre was lost and no longer receives visitors from the land of the Kittim.
